duck_curve.basis: median hour, local time, RAW panel

forecast_weather.lead_alignment_caveat: previous_dayN is the run issued N days earlier; runs are daily, so the effective lead for a given hour is between 24N and 24N+24 hours. The measured degradation is therefore an UPPER bound on the penalty at h=24N.
forecast_weather.source: Open-Meteo previous-runs API (archived operational model runs)

price_status_by_zone.ERCO: BLOCKED: apiexplorer.ercot.com -> HTTP 403 from this network, so no subscription key can be obtained (checked 2026-09-05). Loader also reports: No ERCOT credentials. Register free at https://apiexplorer.e

BPAT.why: Portland — BPA's dominant load centre; hydro and Columbia Gorge wind sit upstream of it.

CISO.why: Los Angeles — the largest load centre inside CAISO; the LA basin drives the summer cooling peak.

ERCO.why: Dallas-Fort Worth — the largest ERCOT metro; Houston is comparable and more humid, and is the named sensitivity check.

MISO.why: Minneapolis — MISO's winter-peaking northern load. The weakest of the six choices: MISO spans to Louisiana.

NYIS.why: New York City — NYISO Zone J is the load concentration; upstate is hydro-rich and much colder.

SWPP.why: Oklahoma City — central to the SPP footprint and close to the wind corridor that sets its net load.

predictions: P1: holdout MAE rises monotonically with the horizon, and the h=1 -> h=24 step is the largest single jump of the three
P2: lag168 ranks below the daily anchor in permutation importance at h=1 and h=24, and above it at h=72 -- the crossover is the finding, not the ranking
P3: MAE is worst in the evening ramp hours (17-21 local) at every horizon
P4: scaled error (MAE / mean net load) is highest for SWPP and lowest for NYIS
P5: temperature's share of permutation importance rises with the horizon

baselines.g2_note: EIA publishes a day-ahead DEMAND forecast, not a net-load forecast. G2 is evaluated against DF minus 24h persistence of wind and solar, which is the best a public-data operator holds at a 24h origin.

classification.label_rule: renewable_share > zone p85 AND net_load < zone p15

nb04.per_horizon_fairness_note: EIA publishes a day-ahead demand forecast only, so at h=48 and h=72 the benchmark holds better demand information than the model. Skill at those horizons is a lower bound; the comparison is fair only at h=24.

p5.caveat: ERA5 reanalysis = perfect weather foresight; upper bound only

search.escalation_withheld_reason: max_iter's range is justified by a measured one-at-a-time sweep (800 is the minimum, 2000 is 11 MW worse, 4000 is 33 MW worse). A win at its ceiling is a plateau bounded on compute, not a range chosen too narrowly.
search.refinement_scope_note: The refining grid spans only the two axes with a measured span larger than the fold noise floor. The other three were searched by the randomised notebook and left unrefined: on 2026-08-22 the full five-axis grid cost 86% of the search's compute for 5.4 MW.

nb06.lower_bound_reason: Only temp is perturbed -- it is the only variable with a published NWP error curve here. Humidity, wind_speed and cloud_cover stay at reanalysis truth, and cloud_cover drives the midday solar belly, so the bound is loosest exactly where the duck curve is.

1.note: no sub-daily forecast archive; nowcast ~ observation

nb06.operational_weather_lead_caveat: previous_dayN is the run issued N days earlier and runs are daily, so the effective lead for a given hour is 24N to 24N+24 hours. Every penalty here is an UPPER bound on the true penalty at h=24N.

nb08.conditional_reserve_verdict: a null on average and a real gain in the distribution: 3.7% more capacity at the same 5% shortfall rate, placed where the risk is, which is the evening ramp

systematic: MAE peaks at local hour 16

nb08.reserve_price_is_a_proxy: spinning reserve is a contingency product sized from the largest single credible outage, not from forecast error; every dollar figure is an upper bound
